title: Xbox Denies Landing Exclusive Streaming Deal For GTA 6 At Launch
summary: Update: "The game will not be streaming exclusively or to PC"
text: Xbox Denies Landing Exclusive Streaming Deal For GTA 6 At Launch | Pure Xbox Menu Search Share Guest Guest Login | Sign Up Pure Xbox News Reviews Features Games Guides Videos Forums Search Keywords Guest Login or Sign Up Home Choose Topics... Manage Topics News Xbox GTA 6 Xbox Cloud Gaming Reports Xbox Denies Landing Exclusive Streaming Deal For GTA 6 At Launch Update: "The game will not be streaming exclusively or to PC" by Fraser Gilbert 4 hours ago Share: Update [ Wed 7th Oct 2026, 8:21am ]: Xbox CSO Matthew Ball has now commented on this report, denying that Xbox has landed an "exclusive" streaming deal, although his wording suggests the game may still be available through Xbox Cloud Gaming. The Verge's Tom Warren later apologised for the confusion caused by his initial article, highlighting that the situation "appears to be more complicated" than initially believed. These things can happen, folks! Here's a look at Xbox's statement: While the excitement for GTAVI and XBOX is great to see, it has also led to some misreporting. We are looking forward to launching GTAVI on XBOX November 19, though the game will not be streaming exclusively or to PC. - Matthew Ball (@ballmatthew) October 7, 2026 Original Story: The biggest deal in Xbox Cloud Gaming history is reportedly just around the corner, as Xbox boss Asha Sharma has apparently told employees that GTA 6 will stream exclusively as part of Xbox Cloud Gaming at launch in November. This news was broken today by The Verge , which says that it doesn't know how long the deal lasts for, but Sharma highlighted that it's something "no other platform holder is doing". "According to sources familiar with Microsoft’s plans, Xbox has managed to land a deal for the exclusive game streaming rights for Grand Theft Auto VI." Xbox's exclusive streaming rights mean that not only will PC players have a way to play GTA 6 ahead of its native PC release, but even Xbox One owners should be able to stream the game to their last-gen consoles as well. One of the catches is that Xbox recently announced Xbox Cloud Gaming streaming limits for Game Pass members that will go into effect from November onwards, with even XGP Ultimate members only getting a maximum of 15 cloud hours per-month unless they're willing to pay for more. It's also claimed that a new pay-as-you-go offering for the service will begin rolling out in November, allowing you to pay for a "bundle of hours" without needing to be a Game Pass subscriber or even own an Xbox console at all. That said, you'll presumably still need to buy the full-priced Xbox console version of GTA 6 before you can access it via the cloud. These limits are starting to make sense now! Xbox Cloud Gaming is going to receive a huge influx of players in November when GTA 6 begins rolling out, so Microsoft better hope its servers can handle the load.
